key_insight: The anomalous γ-loop in Fe–Cr alloys emerges from competing magnetic, vibrational and chemical effects that make Cr favor fcc only within a limited temperature–composition window.
engineering_relevance: Capturing these coupled effects can improve first-principles predictions of fcc–bcc stability in Fe–Cr alloy design.
method: Coupled atomistic spin dynamics with ab initio molecular dynamics.
Used thermodynamic integration to calculate fcc–bcc Gibbs free-energy differences.
Compared magnetically ordered and disordered states to interpret Cr-dependent phase stability.
evidence_signal: Simulations at 0, 5, 10 and 15 at.% Cr over 800–1800 K reproduced the experimental γ-loop trend, with near-quantitative γ–δ transition accuracy.
watch_item: The α–γ transition temperatures were underestimated by approximately 200 K, and clustering remains a proposed explanation for the loop closing from below.
paper_title: Origin of the anomalous shape of the $γ$-loop in paramagnetic Fe1-xCrx alloys from coupled Atomistic Spin Dynamics and ab initio Molecular Dynamics
